headline: Mandatory Backcountry Briefings and Permits
reservation: Front-country camping at Tombstone Mountain Campground is often first-come, first-served, but backcountry sites like Grizzly Lake require advanced reservations. All backcountry users must attend a mandatory orientation at the Tombstone Interpretive Centre to receive their permit and bear-resistant canisters. Systems for these reservations typically open in early spring; verify exact dates and procedures on the Yukon Government website.

days.title: The Dempster Highway Ascent

stops.name: Tombstone Interpretive Centre
stops.detail: Register for your visit, view permafrost exhibits, and check the latest wildlife sighting board.

stops.name: North Fork Pass Summit
stops.detail: Stop at the highest point of the Dempster Highway for a panoramic view of the continental divide and jagged peaks.

days.driving: Allow 1.5–2.5 hours; conditions vary based on gravel road grading
days.note: The Dempster Highway is an unpaved industrial road; watch for heavy trucks and flying stones.

days.title: Alpine Tundra and Valleys

stops.name: Goldensides Trail
stops.detail: A manageable hike offering expansive views of the North Klondike River Valley and volcanic landscapes.

stops.name: Grizzly Creek
stops.detail: Explore the lower elevations of the valley where the boreal forest gives way to the vast shrubs of the tundra.

days.driving: Minimal driving; localized parking at trailheads
days.note: Weather can change from sun to snow within an hour, even in August.

days.title: The Arctic Circle View
days.start: Suggested: 7:30 AM from the Interpretive Centre

stops.name: Two Moose Lake
stops.detail: A prime spot for birdwatching and potential moose sightings in the marshy plateau.

stops.name: Chapman Lake
stops.detail: Observe the largest lake in the park, set against the backdrop of the Mackenzie Mountains.

days.note: Ensure your vehicle has at least one full-sized spare tire before heading north of the Interpretive Centre.

intel.title: Dawson City Supply
intel.text: The last reliable fuel station is in Dawson City or at the start of the Dempster. There is no fuel available within the park boundaries or for a significant distance north.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: Parking at the Grizzly Lake trailhead is limited and often fills during the peak fall color season in late August. Use the overflow areas designated by park staff near the Interpretive Centre.

intel.title: No Cellular Service
intel.text: There is no cell phone coverage along the Dempster Highway or within the park. The Interpretive Centre may have limited emergency radio contact, but personal satellite devices are recommended.

intel.title: Dempster Highway Conditions
intel.text: Road conditions are highly dependent on weather; rain can make the calcium-chloride surface extremely slick. Check the Yukon 511 system for road closures or construction delays.

intel.title: Autumn in August
intel.text: The famous red and gold tundra colors peak very early, usually between the last week of August and the first week of September. Snow is possible any month of the year.

plan.arrival: Fly into Dawson City (YDA), rent a highway-approved vehicle, and stock up on bear-safe food storage and supplies before heading to the Dempster Highway.
plan.vehicle: Check rental agreements specifically for the Dempster Highway; many standard contracts prohibit this road. High-clearance vehicles with two spare tires are the regional standard.
plan.goldenHour: North Fork Pass offers dramatic long shadows across the tundra during the late-night summer sunset.
